Let specific gravities& of concrete and sawdust are $ρ{}_{1}$ and $ρ{}_{2}$ respectively.

$\dfrac{4}{3} \pi \left(R^{3} - r^{3}\right) {ρ}_{1} \text{g} + \dfrac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} {ρ}_{2} \text{g} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^{3} \times 1 \times \text{g}$

$⇒ \dfrac{R^{3} - r^{3}}{r^{3}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} + 1}{{ρ}_{1} - 1} ⇒ \dfrac{\left(R^{3} - r^{3}\right) {ρ}_{1}}{r^{3} {ρ}_{2}} = ( \dfrac{1 - {ρ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1} - 1} ) \dfrac{{ρ}_{1}}{{ρ}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\text{Mass of concrete}}{\text{Mass of saw dust}} = ( \dfrac{1 - 0 \text{.} 3}{2 \text{.} 4 - 1} ) \times \dfrac{2 \text{.} 4}{\text{0} \text{.} 3} = 4$

questions.q: A very light, rectangular wire-frame of dimensions $7cm \times 5cm$ hangs just above the free surface of a liquid of surface tension $T$, with its plane parallel to the free surface. The wire-frame is just brought in contact with the liquid surface and then, lifted up. If the force required to lift the wire-frame is $3 . 36N$, then what is the value of $T$ (in $N{m}^{- 1}$)?
questions.solution:
The downward force of surface tension acting on the wire frame is

${F}_{surfacetension} = T \times l$, where $l$ is the total length of the wire which is in contact with the liquid.

Now since it is a wire frame, the free surface of the liquid will be in contact with the inner as well as the outer perimeter of the wire.

Hence, $l = 2 \times 2 \times \left(7 + 5\right) = 48cm$

$T \times \dfrac{48}{100} = 3 . 36N$

$⇒ T = 7N{m}^{- 1}$

questions.solution:
Let the radii of the two soap bubble be& $a$ and $b$, respectively, and radius of a single larger bubble be $c$.

As excess pressure for a soap bubble is $\dfrac{4S}{r}$ and external pressure is $p$,

${p}_{i} = p + \dfrac{4S}{r}$

So, ${p}_{a} = p + \dfrac{4S}{a}, {p}_{b} = p + \dfrac{4S}{b}$

and ${p}_{c} = p + \dfrac{4T}{c}$ ...(i)

and& ${V}_{a} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pia^{3}, {V}_{b} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pib^{3}$

and ${V}_{c} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pic^{3}$ ...(ii)

Now, as mass is conserved,

${μ}_{a} + {μ}_{b} = {μ}_{c}$

$i . e . , \dfrac{{p}_{a}{V}_{a}}{R{T}_{a}} + \dfrac{{p}_{b}{V}_{b}}{R{T}_{b}} = \dfrac{{p}_{c}{V}_{c}}{R{T}_{c}} \left(aspV = \muRT\right)$

As the temperature is constant,

$i . e . , {T}_{a} = {T}_{b} = {T}_{c}$

So, ${p}_{a}{V}_{a} + {p}_{b}{V}_{b} = {p}_{c}{V}_{c}$

This, in the light of eqns. (i) and (ii) becomes,

$\left(p + \dfrac{4S}{a}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pia^{3}\right) + \left($ p + $\dfrac{4S}{b}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pib^{3}\right) = \left(p + \dfrac{4S}{c}\right)\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pic^{3}\right)$

$i . e . , 4S \left($ a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}\right) = p $\left($ c^{3} - a^{3} - b^{3}\right)$ ...(iii)

Now,& $V = $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left($ a^{3} + b^{3} - c^{3}\right)$

and $A = $4\pi \left($ a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}\right)$

$∴ $\dfrac{SA}{\pi} = - \dfrac{3Vp}{4\pi}$

or $4SA + 3pV = 0$

$∴$    Loss in the gravitational potential energy $= {\left(\dfrac{{\text{h}}_{1} - {\text{h}}_{2}}{2}\right)}^{2} \text{A} ρg$

Equating energies, we get $v = \left({\text{h}}_{1} - {\text{h}}_{2}\right)\sqrt{\dfrac{\text{g}}{2\left({\text{h}}_{1} + {\text{h}}_{2} + \text{h}\right)}}$

questions.q: A concrete sphere of the radius $R$ has a cavity of radius$r$ which is packed with sawdust. The specific gravities of concrete and sawdust are respectively $2 . 4$ and $0 . 3$ For this sphere to float with its entire volume submerged underwater, the ratio of the mass of concrete to the mass of sawdust will be
questions.solution:
Let specific gravities of concrete and sawdust are $ρ{}_{1}$ and $ρ{}_{2}$ respectively.
According to principle of floatation, weight of whole sphere = upthrust on the sphere

$\dfrac{4}{3} \pi \left({\text{R}}^{3} - {\text{r}}^{3}\right) {ρ}_{1} \text{g} + \dfrac{4}{3} \pi {\text{r}}^{3} {ρ}_{2} \text{g} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi {\text{R}}^{3} \times 1 \times \text{g}$

$⇒ {\text{R}}^{3} {ρ}_{1} - {\text{r}}^{3} {ρ}_{1} + {\text{r}}^{3} {ρ}_{2} = {\text{R}}^{3}$

$⇒ {\text{R}}^{3} \left({ρ}_{1} - 1\right) = {\text{r}}^{3} \left({ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{{\text{R}}^{3}}{{\text{r}}^{3}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1} - 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\text{R}}^{3} - {\text{r}}^{3}}{{\text{r}}^{3}} = \dfrac{{ρ}_{1} - {ρ}_{2} - {ρ}_{1} + 1}{{ρ}_{1} - 1} ⇒ \dfrac{\left({\text{R}}^{3} - {\text{r}}^{3}\right) {ρ}_{1}}{{\text{r}}^{3} {ρ}_{2}} = ( \dfrac{1 - {ρ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{1} - 1} ) \dfrac{{ρ}_{1}}{{ρ}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\text{Mass of concrete}}{\text{Mass of saw dust}} = ( \dfrac{1 - 0 \text{.} 3}{2 \text{.} 4 - 1} ) \times \dfrac{2 \text{.} 4}{\text{0} \text{.} 3} = 4$
